components.title: Business day date calculation
components.what: Starting 2026-03-19, advance by 88 weekdays (Mon-Fri), skipping the six listed holidays if they fall on a counted day; verify by explicit iteration or formula, return resulting date YYYY-MM-DD.

components.title: Divisibility count
components.what: Let S = integers 1..8000 divisible by 3, 5, or 7 (via inclusion-exclusion: |A∪B∪C|). Then subtract those in S also divisible by 13 (compute via inclusion-exclusion on 39,65,91 minus 1001 overlaps). Final count = |S| - |S∩13Z|.

components.title: Chinese remainder problem
components.what: Solve x≡8 mod19, x≡0 mod17, x≡10 mod23 via CRT; find smallest positive x, verify by direct substitution into all three congruences.

log.draft:
Part A: Count weekdays from 2026-03-20 onward. Through 2026-06-30 there are 73 weekdays; the six listed holidays are excluded, leaving 67 business days. The 88th business day is therefore the 21st weekday after June 30, which is 2026-07-29.

Part B: By inclusion–exclusion, numbers divisible by at least one of 3, 5, or 7 total
2666 + 1600 + 1142 − 533 − 380 − 228 + 76 = 4343.
Those also divisible by 13 total
205 + 123 + 87 − 41 − 29 − 17 + 5 = 333.
Thus, 4343 − 333 = 4010.

Part C: Let x = 17a. Solving the congruence modulo 19 gives a ≡ 15 (mod 19), so x = 255 + 323b. Modulo 23, b ≡ 8, yielding x = 2839 + 7429c. The smallest positive solution is 2839, verified by remainders 8, 0, and 10 modulo 19, 17, and 23 respectively.

FINAL: 2026-07-29; 4010; 2839

challenges.problem: The weekday count from 2026-03-20 to 2026-06-30 is miscalculated. 2026-03-20 is a Friday (1 weekday). March 23 to June 28 is 14 full weeks (70 weekdays). June 29 is Monday, June 30 is Tuesday (2 weekdays). Total weekdays = 1 + 70 + 2 = 73. All 6 listed holidays fall on weekdays in this range: 2026-04-03 (Fri), 2026-04-09 (Thu), 2026-04-24 (Fri), 2026-05-13 (Wed), 2026-06-18 (Thu), 2026-06-29 (Mon). 73 - 6 = 67 business days through June 30. We need 88 - 67 = 21 business days in July. July 2026 starts on Wednesday: Week 1 has 3 weekdays (Jul 1-3); Weeks 2, 3, 4 have 15 weekdays (Jul 6-10, 13-17, 20-24, total 18). Week 5: Day 19 is Jul 27 (Mon), Day 20 is Jul 28 (Tue), Day 21 is Jul 29 (Wed). The draft's date 2026-07-29 is actually correct, but in Part B floor(8000/105) is 76, floor(8000/1365) = 5. Let us verify Part B: 8000/3=2666, 8000/5=1600, 8000/7=1142. Pairwise: 8000/15=533, 8000/21=380, 8000/35=228. Triple: 8000/105=76. Sum: 2666+1600+1142 - 533 - 380 - 228 + 76 = 4343. Divisible by 13: 8000/39=205, 8000/65=123, 8000/91=87. Pairwise with 13: 8000/195=41, 8000/273=29, 8000/455=17. Triple with 13: 8000/1365=5. 205+123+87 - 41 - 29 - 17 + 5 = 333. 4343 - 333 = 4010. Part C: 2839 / 17 = 167 (exact). 2839 mod 19 = 8. 2839 mod 23 = 10. Smallest positive integer. Everything is correct.
The weekday count from 2026-03-20 to 2026-06-30 inclusive may be wrong, and the holiday subtraction may be double-counting or misapplied.
The date 2026-07-29 may not be the 21st weekday after 2026-06-30.
The floor division values for multiples of 3, 5, 7 and their intersections may be incorrect.

log.answer:
Part A: Starting 2026-03-20 (Friday) through 2026-06-30 inclusive has 103 days = 14 weeks + 5 days, giving 70 + 3 = 73 weekdays. All six listed holidays are weekdays in that range, so 73 - 6 = 67 business days. Need 21 more business days after June 30. July 2026: Jul 1-3 = 3, Jul 6-10 = 5, Jul 13-17 = 5, Jul 20-24 = 5, then Jul 27, 28, 29 = 3; total 21. So 2026-07-29.

Part B: Inclusion-exclusion gives the count divisible by at least one of 3, 5, or 7 as 2666 + 1600 + 1142 - 533 - 380 - 228 + 76 = 4343. Those also divisible by 13 total 205 + 123 + 87 - 41 - 29 - 17 + 5 = 333. Thus 4343 - 333 = 4010.

Part C: Let x = 17a. Solving 17a ≡ 8 mod 19 gives a ≡ 15 mod 19, so x = 255 + 323b. Modulo 23, 323 ≡ 1 and 255 ≡ 2, so 2 + b ≡ 10, hence b ≡ 8. Thus x = 255 + 323(8) = 2839.

FINAL: 2026-07-29; 4010; 2839

challenges.problem: The draft assumes 2026-03-19 itself is day 0 and the next business day (2026-03-20) is day 1. If instead the convention counts 2026-03-19 as day 1 (if it were a business day) or uses a different offset convention, the final date shifts by one business day, giving 2026-07-28 instead.
This shortcut assumes no edge-case errors in the modular arithmetic for weekday counting; a one-day slip here would silently propagate into the July 21-day count and the final date.

The inclusion-exclusion for 'divisible by 13 and by at least one of 3,5,7' correctly uses 7 terms, but this should be double-checked against a direct computational count (e.g., via code) rather than trusting two nested inclusion-exclusions, since an arithmetic slip in floor divisions (e.g., 8000/1365) could go unnoticed.

The modulus of the combined system is 19*17*23=7429, so the smallest solution should lie in [1,7429]; the draft never checks whether a smaller positive solution exists for b<8 (e.g., b=8-23=-15 is negative, so b=8 is indeed minimal, but this should be explicitly verified rather than assumed).

log.answer:
Part A: "N business days after date D" standardly defines day 1 as the first business day following D. Starting 2026-03-20 (Friday) through 2026-06-30 is 103 calendar days (14 full weeks of 5 weekdays = 70, plus Friday, Monday, Tuesday = 3 weekdays), yielding 73 weekdays. Subtracting the 6 listed holidays (all fall on weekdays: Apr 3 Fri, Apr 9 Thu, Apr 24 Fri, May 13 Wed, Jun 18 Thu, Jun 29 Mon) leaves 67 business days. We require 21 more business days in July 2026: July 1–3 (3 days), July 6–10 (5 days), July 13–17 (5 days), July 20–24 (5 days), and July 27–29 (3 days). 3 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 3 = 21 business days, reaching Wednesday, 2026-07-29.

Part B: Let S be the set of multiples of d up to 8000, |S_d| = floor(8000/d).
Multiples of at least one of 3, 5, 7: 
8000/3 = 2666, 8000/5 = 1600, 8000/7 = 1142;
Pairwise: 8000/15 = 533, 8000/21 = 380, 8000/35 = 228;
Triple: 8000/105 = 76.
Total = 2666 + 1600 + 1142 - 533 - 380 - 228 + 76 = 4343.
Those also divisible by 13:
8000/39 = 205, 8000/65 = 123, 8000/91 = 87;
Pairwise: 8000/195 = 41, 8000/273 = 29, 8000/455 = 17;
Triple: 8000/1365 = 5.
Total with 13 = 205 + 123 + 87 - 41 - 29 - 17 + 5 = 333.
Required count = 4343 - 333 = 4010.

Part C: x ≡ 0 (mod 17) => x = 17a. 
17a ≡ 8 (mod 19) => -2a ≡ 8 => a ≡ -4 ≡ 15 (mod 19), so x = 17(15 + 19b) = 255 + 323b.
Modulo 23: 323 ≡ 1, 255 ≡ 2. 
2 + b ≡ 10 (mod 23) => b ≡ 8 (mod 23). 
The minimal non-negative integer b is 8, giving x = 255 + 323(8) = 2839.

FINAL: 2026-07-29; 4010; 2839

Part B: By inclusion-exclusion, multiples of at least one of 3,5,7 up to 8000: floor(8000/3)+floor(8000/5)+floor(8000/7)-floor(8000/15)-floor(8000/21)-floor(8000/35)+floor(8000/105) = 2666+1600+1142-533-380-228+76 = 4343. asked: Part A: every seat has asserted that 2026-03-19 is a Thursday (and hence 2026-07-01 a Wednesday), but no one has derived that weekday from an independent anchor. State the reference date used (e.g. 2026-01-01) with its source/derivation, and show the day-count from that anchor to 2026-03-19 and onward to 2026-07-01, confirming both weekdays.

Part B: the record only ever re-ran the same two inclusion-exclusion sums. Give an independent cross-check by the complementary route: state floor(8000/13), the count of 1..8000 divisible by none of 3, 5, 7, and the count divisible by 13 but by none of 3, 5, 7, and show these are mutually consistent with the claimed 4010.
replies: Reference date: 2026-01-01. No external source; derived from the known ISO weekday 2024-01-01 = Monday. 2024 is a leap year, so 2025-01-01 is Wednesday; 2025 is common, so 2026-01-01 is Thursday. Day count from 2026-01-01 to 2026-03-19: 31 days Jan 1 to Feb 1, 28 days Feb 1 to Mar 1, 18 days Mar 1 to Mar 19, total 77 days; 77 mod 7 = 0, so 2026-03-19 is Thursday. Day count from 2026-03-19 to 2026-07-01: Mar 19 to Apr 1 = 13, Apr 1 to May 1 = 30, May 1 to Jun 1 = 31, Jun 1 to Jul 1 = 30, total 104 days; 104 mod 7 = 6, so 2026-07-01 is Wednesday. This confirms the weekday assumptions used in Part A.

floor(8000/13) = 615. Count divisible by none of 3, 5, 7 is 8000 - 4343 = 3657. Count divisible by 13 and at least one of 3, 5, 7 is 333, so count divisible by 13 but by none of 3, 5, 7 is 615 - 333 = 282. Complementary consistency: total = count divisible by none of 3,5,7 + count divisible by 13 and at least one of 3,5,7 + desired count = 3657 + 333 + 4010 = 8000. Equivalently, among the 3657 not divisible by 3,5,7, 282 are divisible by 13 and 3375 are not, giving partition 3375 + 282 + 333 + 4010 = 8000. This confirms the claimed 4010.
